# duploai_network_baseline_security_group_rule (Data Source)

Manages one inbound rule on a duploai_network_baseline's primary AWS security group — the network-scoped sibling of duploai_resource_group_security_group_rule. Each resource is a single rule with exactly one source: an IPv4 CIDR, an IPv6 CIDR, or a resource group whose own security group becomes the source. Declare several blocks for several rules. AWS assigns each rule an id, which is what Terraform tracks and what the API updates and deletes by.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Look up an existing inbound rule by its AWS security group rule ID.
data "duploai_network_baseline_security_group_rule" "existing" {
  workspace_id = "<workspace-id>"
  network_id   = "<network-id>"
  id           = "sgr-0123456789abcdef0"
}

output "rule_protocol" {
  value = data.duploai_network_baseline_security_group_rule.existing.ip_protocol
}

# Exactly one of these is populated, depending on the rule's source type.
output "rule_source" {
  value = coalesce(
    data.duploai_network_baseline_security_group_rule.existing.cidr_ipv4,
    data.duploai_network_baseline_security_group_rule.existing.cidr_ipv6,
    data.duploai_network_baseline_security_group_rule.existing.referenced_group_id,
  )
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) ID of the object to look up.
- `network_id` (String) ID of the duploai_network_baseline whose primary security group this rule is added to. Read it from that resource's network_id attribute. The network is workspace-scoped, so no environment or resource group is involved.
- `workspace_id` (String) ID of the workspace that owns the network.

### Read-Only

- `cidr_ipv4` (String) IPv4 CIDR allowed by this rule, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8 or 203.0.113.4/32. Exactly one source is required: cidr_ipv4, cidr_ipv6, or source_resource_group_id.
- `cidr_ipv6` (String) IPv6 CIDR allowed by this rule, e.g. 2001:db8::/64. Exactly one source is required: cidr_ipv4, cidr_ipv6, or source_resource_group_id.
- `description` (String) Free-text description for the rule. The platform applies it to the rule's source entry, so it appears on the rule in the AWS console.
- `from_port` (Number) Start of the allowed port range for tcp/udp (1-65535), or the ICMP type for icmp/icmpv6 where -1 means all types. Required for tcp and udp.
- `group_id` (String) ID of the security group the rule belongs to — the resource group's primary security group.
- `ip_protocol` (String) IP protocol the rule allows: tcp, udp, icmp, icmpv6, or -1 for all protocols. from_port and to_port are required for tcp and udp; for icmp and icmpv6 they carry the ICMP type and code and default to -1 (all types, all codes) when omitted; for -1 they are ignored.
- `referenced_group_id` (String) ID of the source security group, when the source is another security group. Populated when source_resource_group_id is set.
- `security_group_rule_arn` (String) ARN of this security group rule.
- `security_group_rule_id` (String) AWS-assigned id of this rule (sgr-...). The API updates and deletes rules by this value.
- `source_resource_group_id` (String) ID of a resource group whose primary security group is the source of this rule — the platform resolves it to that group's sg- id. The referenced group must be in the same workspace as the network and must already have its security group provisioned. Exactly one source is required: cidr_ipv4, cidr_ipv6, or source_resource_group_id.
- `to_port` (Number) End of the allowed port range for tcp/udp (1-65535), or the ICMP code for icmp/icmpv6 where -1 means all codes. Required for tcp and udp, and must be greater than or equal to from_port.
